notes: Semantic Student Intent Interpreter (PR 2) offline evaluation corpus. Every case is run deterministically (mode="off") against the typed StudentIntent contract with zero model calls — see tests/test_student_intent_eval_fixture.py. For cases where expectedEscalates=true, the fixture test also monkeypatches the semantic call (never a real network call) to verify fail-closed fallback reproduces the same fields, and checks downstream execution_router.resolve_execution_plan compatibility. Real live-model accuracy evaluation (does the MODEL's judgment match expectedPrimaryTask when actually invoked) requires separate authorization for paid calls — not run here.

cases.message: Explain the concept on this page in detail. Do not summarize it.
cases.expectedBehavior: The historical regression this whole initiative exists to fix: primary_task must NOT become course_summary just because a prohibition mentions it; course_summary must appear in prohibited_tasks instead.

cases.message: Explain Newton's third law. Do not quiz me on it.
cases.expectedBehavior: Quiz prohibition recorded without being the primary task. Escalates because NEGATED_QUIZ_RE matches "do not quiz me on it"; needs_clarification is true because the trailing "it" trips the deictic check with no active exercise label or visible context to anchor it.

cases.message: Summarize chapter 3 briefly.
cases.expectedBehavior: A plain positive request must not be flagged as prohibited anywhere (the prohibition machinery must not over-fire).

cases.message: Fasse Kapitel 3 kurz zusammen.
cases.expectedBehavior: German-phrased summarize task classifies the same as its English equivalent.

cases.message: Summarize this chapter. Do not summarize it.
cases.expectedBehavior: Genuinely self-contradictory input must never let primary_task collide with prohibited_tasks (invariant 2) — the deterministic adapter already degrades to general_course_qa rather than picking either contradictory instruction; this is also exactly the shape _semantic_model_call's own primaryTask/prohibitedTasks conflict check guards against if the model were to try to resolve the contradiction by name.

cases.message: Erkläre das Konzept auf dieser Seite im Detail. Fasse es nicht zusammen.
cases.expectedBehavior: German translation of the historical BWL case — the regression fix must hold in German too, and the diacritics alone (no ASCII/non-ASCII mix here) do not spuriously trigger the code-switch heuristic; it escalates because of the negation, not the language.

cases.message: What is the formula for torsion?
cases.expectedBehavior: Plain English factual question — unambiguous, deterministic path only.

cases.message: Please erkläre mir die Übung in English, kurz und präzise.
cases.expectedBehavior: ASCII English words mixed with German diacritics in one message must trigger escalation via the code-switch heuristic (_ASCII_LETTERS_RE + _NON_ASCII_LETTERS_RE) — a case the two narrow negation regexes would never catch, since there is no negation here at all.

cases.message: Why did you divide by J?

previousTurns.text: Calculate the torsion for this shaft.

cases.expectedBehavior: A follow-up question about the previous answer sets follow_up_type and a brief depth; high lexical confidence means no escalation is needed.

cases.message: No, that's wrong.
cases.expectedBehavior: A correction/rejection always escalates (dialogue.relation in {CORRECTION, REJECTION}), regardless of lexical confidence, because the deterministic adapter alone cannot tell WHAT was wrong about the prior answer.

cases.message: No, that's wrong.
cases.expectedBehavior: When the semantic call raises on malformed/out-of-schema output, interpret_student_intent must fail closed to interpretation_source="fallback" with the SAME fields as the deterministic base — never propagate the exception.

cases.message: Please erkläre mir die Übung in English, kurz und präzise.
cases.expectedBehavior: A provider timeout on the code-switched path must fail closed exactly like malformed output — same fallback contract, different exception type.

cases.message: Draw a free-body diagram for this beam.
cases.expectedBehavior: visual_requirement must be true; scope stays the router's trusted VISIBLE_PAGE access, never re-derived from the message.

cases.message: What does it say on page 6?
cases.expectedBehavior: A page reference resolves via trusted visible-page context (has_visible_context=true), never by parsing "page 6" out of the message text (invariant 4).

cases.message: Quiz me on the chapter about thermodynamics.
cases.expectedBehavior: Plain quiz request, unambiguous.

cases.message: Quiz me on thermodynamics but do not show me the answers yet.
cases.expectedBehavior: PR3 ADJUDICATION (was knownGap, now fixed): "do not show me the answers yet" is detected by the new deterministic _WITHHOLD_ANSWER_RE into StudentIntent.answer_constraints.withhold_answer=True, independent of NEGATED_QUIZ_RE/prohibited_tasks (this is "quiz me but hide the answer", not "do not quiz me" — the two must never be confused). Still does not trip _needs_semantic_path (unchanged, still deterministic-only, still no escalation) — that heuristic-tuning question remains open and is unrelated to whether the constraint reaches the typed contract, which it now does.

cases.message: Can I get a hint for exercise 4.2?

previousTurns.text: Here is the setup for exercise 4.2: F = ma.

cases.expectedBehavior: depth must be "one_step", distinguishing a hint request from a full-solution request. PR3 ADJUDICATION: also now sets answer_constraints.hint_only=True (via dialogue_state.wants_hint_only, reused rather than re-detected) — this is the same underlying signal as the depth check, now additionally exposed as an explicit generation constraint.

cases.message: Solve exercise 5.1 completely, show all steps.
cases.expectedBehavior: Full-solution request classifies as math_problem with normal depth (not one_step), the opposite of the hint case above.

cases.message: Explain Newton's third law of motion.
cases.expectedBehavior: Plain explanation request, unambiguous.

cases.message: Compare torsion and bending stress.
cases.expectedBehavior: Plain comparison request, unambiguous.

cases.message: Explain this to me.
cases.expectedBehavior: No-fabrication invariant: a deictic reference ("this") with no active exercise label and no visible context sets needs_clarification=True rather than guessing. Does not escalate under the current trigger set (dialogue.confidence stays high and there is no negation/code-switch), so this stays a deterministic-only fix — a candidate for widening _needs_semantic_path in a future tuning pass, not this PR.

cases.message: Explain this to me.
cases.expectedBehavior: The SAME deictic message, but trusted visible-page context resolves the reference, so needs_clarification flips to False — contrast with missing-context-deictic above.

cases.message: Explain how entropy relates to the second law of thermodynamics.
cases.expectedBehavior: PR3 ADJUDICATION (was knownGap, now fixed): _DEICTIC_RE's ordinal branch previously matched "the second law" as a deictic back-reference. Fixed with a narrow negative-lookahead exclusion (law/theorem/postulate/principle/rule/equation/formula/axiom/derivative/integral + plurals) right after the ordinal, so "the second law/theorem/..." no longer matches while "the second problem/question/one/part/..." (anything else) still does — confirmed by the sibling cases missing-context-deictic/missing-context-resolved-via-visible-context, which are unaffected. needs_clarification now correctly stays False for this fully self-contained question. Id kept as-is (not relabeled) since the case itself — and the underlying message — is unchanged; only the observed, now-correct behavior changed. German ordinal deixis ("die zweite Aufgabe") remains entirely unhandled by _DEICTIC_RE — a separate, pre-existing gap, not touched here (would be new scope, not a narrow correction).
